real_s1.explanation: The clearest signal is subject size. The unit is much more active when the main subject fills a quarter or more of the frame than when it is small or distant (rows 7 and 8, d about +1.0, 97th-98th percentile). Its similar units share this preference, so it reflects the group's close-up, large-subject tuning rather than something unique to this unit. It may also respond somewhat more when the subject is cut off by the frame edge or sharply focused, but those effects are not unusual for the layer. The color-tint story did not hold up. Warm tint over neutral (row 18) reversed on the new photos. The black-and-white contrasts (rows 20, 22, 23) rest on only about 5 photos and could not be checked, and similar units often score high on them too. So color is not a reliable feature of this unit.

real_s2.explanation: The unit fires most on photos where a single main subject is large and prominent, filling at least a quarter of the frame and often cut off by its edges. Its top classes are mostly patterned animals such as snakes and big cats, plus some machines and instruments. The strongest and most reliable effect is that it responds weakly when the subject is small (less than a quarter of the photo). Similar units share this preference, so it is not unique to this unit. The apparent preference for warm or cool colour casts over neutral photos did not hold on new photos, so it should not be trusted. No other row stands out as particular to this unit.
